local_market_longform:
San Jose is its own market, and a cash sale here works differently than the national talking points suggest. Homes in San Jose currently trade around a median of $1,450,000 and take roughly 22 days to go under contract, with about 25% of area sales closing in cash. When you need certainty instead of a drawn-out listing — a firm number and a date you choose — that local pace is exactly why selling directly makes sense.

The housing stock shapes everything about condition here. San Jose runs heavily to post-war Eichler and ranch tracts, 1970s–1990s subdivisions, and dense newer infill, and each era carries its own repair realities. That matters because we price the house in front of us rather than asking you to renovate it first — the things a traditional buyer's inspector flags are the same things we already expect and account for.

Local conditions are the other factor a generic buyer ignores. Around San Jose, the issues we see most are seismic risk on the Hayward and Calaveras faults, soft-story and unreinforced older homes, and expansive bay-margin soils. We've made offers on homes with every one of those problems, so none of it scares us off or kills the deal at the last minute.

We buy across the whole area — from close-in neighborhoods like East San Jose out to Milpitas and Campbell — and in California the local economy anchored by the core of Silicon Valley tech — Apple, Google, Nvidia, and a dense startup economy keeps demand real. Inherited homes, tired rentals, pre-foreclosure situations in Santa Clara County, and houses that simply need more work than the owner wants to take on: those are the San Jose sellers we help most.

Being a genuinely local buyer near downtown's SAP Center also means our offer isn't a lowball pulled from a national algorithm that has never seen San Jose. We know what a block in East San Jose, Alum Rock, Willow Glen, and Japantown actually sells for, what Silicon Valley buyers will and won't pay for, and how Santa Clara County's title and closing process really works. That local read is why our sellers get a number they can trust and a closing that actually happens on the date we promised.

situations.title: Tired of two mortgages

situations.title: Inherited a house in San Jose
situations.body: Settling an estate — often from out of state — is hard enough without a listing on top of it. We buy inherited San Jose homes as-is, work alongside the Santa Clara County probate process, and let you take what matters and leave the rest.

situations.title: The house needs too much work
situations.body: Fire, water, foundation, or years of deferred repairs — we've bought all of it around San Jose. No cleaning, no contractors, no staging.

situations.title: Downsizing or aging in place
situations.body: When a longtime East San Jose-area home has become too much to keep up, we make a fair offer and let you set a move-out date that isn't rushed.

faq.q: How fast can you close on my San Jose house?
faq.a: As little as 7 days through a licensed California title company, or any later date you choose. Sellers in San Jose pick the timeline that fits their move.

faq.q: Do I pay any fees or commissions?
faq.a: None. No agent commissions, no listing fees, and we cover standard closing costs. The number we agree on is what you receive.

faq.q: Do I need to repair or clean the house first?
faq.a: No. We buy San Jose homes in any condition — including the seismic risk on the Hayward and Calaveras faults we see so often here. Take what you want and leave the rest.

faq.q: How do you decide the offer amount?
faq.a: We look at recent comparable sales in your San Jose neighborhood — places like East San Jose — the home's condition, and current Silicon Valley demand, then make a fair cash offer you're free to accept or decline.

faq.q: Is this a licensed, legitimate way to sell in California?
faq.a: Yes. We are a direct buyer, not your agent or broker, and we put that in writing. California permits direct cash purchases; we market our own equitable interest and disclose our role in writing.

faq.q: Can you help with foreclosure, probate, or tenants?
faq.a: Often, yes. We regularly work with Santa Clara County sellers facing foreclosure, probate, liens, or tenant issues, and we structure the sale around the situation.
